title: incident-bot: rank autodiagnostics suggestions by priority and SLO impact
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: On-call engineers rely on incident-bot autodiagnostics and runbook suggestions during SLO incidents. Currently suggestions are ordered by simple heuristics which often surface low-value actions first. This PR adds a lightweight priority ranking layer that scores suggestions by estimated SLO impact, recent incident context, and historical action effectiveness to surface the most actionable runbooks and diagnostics.

What this PR does: implements a scoring pipeline for autodiagnostics suggestions; augments suggestion payloads with priority metadata; exposes a small configuration surface to tune weighting (slo_impact_weight, recent_context_weight, historical_success_weight); and updates on-call helper commands to display priority and confidence. The implementation is intentionally conservative: default weights favor SLO impact and recency, and the scorer runs as a post-processing step so existing suggestion generation is unchanged.

Files changed overview: changes touch the suggestion ranking service, the incident-bot API response, on-call command output formatting, a couple of unit tests, and documentation + config.

Testing and rollout: unit and integration tests added for ranking logic and edge cases (no context, single suggestion, tied scores). Feature gated behind incident-bot.config.autodiag.priority_ranking (off by default) and toggled for the oncall-dev team for the initial canary. Observability: adds metrics incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.latency and incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.score_distribution; we also emit a sample of ranked suggestions to S3 for offline evaluation.

Related: addresses ENG-1742 (prioritize runbook suggestions) and ENG-1819 (autodiagnostics quality improvements). Backport: small backport PR will be opened to release/2026.01 if canary metrics look good.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests against synthetic incidents
- [x] Metrics and logging added
- [x] Feature flag + config entry
- [x] Documentation and runbook note updated

Notes for reviewers: the scorer is deterministic and pure (no external calls) to keep latency bounded; added microbenchmarks show median scorer CPU cost ~150us per request. The canary rollout plan is in the PR description with target metrics (no regressions in autodiag latency, >10% improvement in suggestion-success rate in canary).

review_comments: Jared Turner (reviewer): Can we make sure the default weights are conservative? We should avoid surfacing noisy runbooks that cause extra pagings.
Priya Nair (author): Yes — defaults favor SLO impact + recency. Added a comment in defaults.yaml and a test to validate defaults remain unchanged.
Lina Gomez (reviewer): Are we concerned about scorer cost at high QPS? We should validate it on a dedicated canary before broad rollout.
Priya Nair (author): Benchmarks show ~150us median CPU; scorer is CPU-only and threads well. I'll add a canary with traffic cap and monitor incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.latency.
Marcus Lee (reviewer): Minor: prefer shorter metric name (autodiag.ranking.latency -> incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.latency) for consistency with other metrics.
Priya Nair (author): Updated metric name and added a migration note in observability/metrics_registry.py.
release_notes: incident-bot: add priority-ranking to autodiagnostics to surface higher-impact runbooks first. Feature gated and off by default. Metrics and config added.
canary_rollout_notes: Enabled for oncall-dev team for 72h canary with traffic cap 5% of autodiag requests. Monitor incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.latency, suggestion_success_rate, and errors. If suggestion_success_rate improves by >=10% and latency regression <5%, start ramp to 25%.
observability_changes: Added metrics: incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.latency, incident_bot.autodiag.ranking.score_distribution. Emits sampled ranked suggestions to s3://redwood-autodiag-samples/ for offline evaluation.
notes: This change is non-breaking and feature gated. Follow-up PR will wire sample consumer for offline evaluation dashboard.
